items.title: CP SSH host-key trust: mandatory strict enforcement for production/container runtime
items.priority: P0 -- production-blocking before production deployment / CLASS 2
items.note: PO decision 2026-09-03 (OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md "CP SSH trust -- PO override, development compatibility mode"): the OP.0b S5 CP HA preflight feature (checkpoint.preflight_collector.run_cp_preflight) defaults strict_host_key=False for the current development/pre-production phase, matching every other CP SSH caller's existing compatibility-mode default -- mandatory strict enforcement is deliberately deferred to the future production/container-pod runtime, not implemented now, to avoid investing in workstation-specific Paramiko trust-management machinery ahead of that migration. Strict mode itself remains fully implemented, fail-closed and selectable today via strict_host_key=True; utils.cp_ssh_trust.apply_strict_host_key_policy is unchanged. This item is the production checklist for closing that deferral. Scope: (1) mandatory strict host-key verification for the production runtime -- no compatibility-mode default once containerized; (2) container/pod known_hosts provisioning mechanism (bind-mount or equivalent, matching deploy/secrets/ conventions); (3) independently verified host-key enrollment/provisioning procedure -- no TOFU, no ssh-keyscan-as-trust, out-of-band fingerprint verification required; (4) host-key rotation procedure; (5) mismatch handling (BadHostKeyException stays a distinct, non-retryable, fail-closed rejection); (6) missing-host-key handling (HostKeyNotTrustedError stays a distinct, non-retryable, fail-closed rejection -- see host-key-retry-classification finding below); (7) no automatic promotion of an OBSERVED_UNVERIFIED compatibility-mode fingerprint to trusted status, ever; (8) production startup/preflight should positively prove trusted host-key material exists before the runtime is considered ready, not merely fail closed on first connection attempt; (9) migration away from workstation-specific trust assumptions (a developer's own ~/.ssh/known_hosts) toward a runtime-owned, deployment-provisioned trust store. Host-key-retry-classification finding folded in here rather than a separate item: op0b_s8_host_key_retry_classification (HostKeyNotTrustedError, merged 2026-09-03, PR #47) already made a missing-host-key rejection non-retryable in both CP SSH retry loops; this item tracks keeping that guarantee true as production hardening proceeds, not redoing it. Reconciled with, not duplicating, the narrower cp_ssh_trust_r2_prod_server item (DEPLOY.1 Ubuntu/Docker server R2 validation for the existing CP config-collection path) -- that item's obligation is one line item under this broader checklist. Do not claim strict production hardening is complete until this item closes; the current state is deliberately, explicitly INCOMPLETE by PO decision, not a regression.

items.title: Render harness's happy-dom check failed under Bun (window.eval undefined)
items.target: before RB.5 (or any next UI build)
items.note: AUTOMATED_VALIDATED 2026-08-31 (contract: docs/history/phase/PHASE0_6_X_RENDER_HARNESS_HAPPYDOM_PIN.md). Root cause was NOT a happy-dom version regression as originally suspected 2026-08-30 -- it is a Bun/node:vm incompatibility. happy-dom executes each Window's script inside a node:vm context; under Bun that context's globals come back broken (window.eval is an own property whose value is simply undefined -- 'TypeError: window.eval is not a function' -- and even built-ins like Map/Error resolve to undefined inside a script run there). Reproduced identically on every happy-dom major tested (16.0.0, 19.0.2, 20.12.0) under Bun; the exact same happy-dom 20.12.0 works correctly under real Node.js (window.eval is a real function, normal global semantics) with zero code change to check-render.mjs. A dead-end explored and reverted before finding this: happy-dom's newer enableJavaScriptEvaluation setting does make document.write()-inserted <script> tags auto-execute without window.eval, but even that runs each script in its own isolated scope (top-level function/var declarations do not attach to window) -- not usable for this harness's needs (window.switchModule must be reachable), so that direction was abandoned, not shipped. items.target: CON.0 (architecture, frozen 2026-08-31) -> CON.1 (DONE, 2026-09-01) -> CON.2 (AUTOMATED_VALIDATED, 2026-09-01; real-env owed) -> CON.3..CON.5
items.note: ARCHITECTURE FROZEN 2026-08-31 (docs/design/OPERATOR_CONSOLE_ARCHITECTURE.md) with all five phase contracts written in the same pass: CON_1_OPERATOR_CONSOLE_READ_ONLY.md, CON_2_CONSOLE_JOB_ENGINE_READ_ACTIONS.md, CON_3_CONSOLE_OPERATIONAL_WRITE_ACTIONS.md, CON_4_CONSOLE_RECOVERY_MODULE.md, CON_5_CONSOLE_SCHEDULER_SURFACE.md (all under docs/history/phase/). Driver: the BackBox exit (BACKUP_AND_RECOVERY_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2) needs an operator surface, not just a capability -- BackBox's daily value is seeing the fleet and acting on a row, which today requires the CLI. Central decision: do NOT make the exported report dynamic. The portable, shareable, action-free output/index.html is a product feature; the console is a SECOND delivery surface over the same engine, sharing one UI source tree (mode flag SECURITYEXPERT_MODE) and one orchestration core. Security boundary: the browser sends intent (a job_type resolved against a closed, source-resident registry plus entity ids validated against unified.json), never a device command, flag or argv fragment -- which is how this stays inside SERVER_PRODUCTIZATION_AND_MODULARIZATION_ARCHITECTURE.md's prohibitions on a generic REST wrapper and browser-supplied commands (that doc is amended with a section 7 reconciliation, prohibitions unrelaxed). The console adds exactly four things - an HTTP boundary, an auth boundary, a durable job record and one new provenance value - and no new device path: execution reuses main(argv, runtime_services, provenance) the way the scheduler already does (main.py:361), plus CollectionCoordinator admission and the 24h operational-write ledger unchanged. Hard ordering: CON.1 was blocked on codebase_modularization (frontend) being DONE (it changes app_bootstrap.js initialization to initializeReport(payloads)) -- cleared 2026-09-01; CON.3 is blocked on RB.3b reaching REAL_ENV_VALIDATED -- a UI must never be the first thing to run a device write nobody has run by hand. C-D1/C-D2 (project/roadmap.json open_decisions) were approved 2026-09-01 per their documented recommendations: optional fastapi+uvicorn dependency (requirements-console.txt), cookieless per-launch bearer token in the URL fragment. CON.1 SHIPPED 2026-09-01: `console/` package (auth.py, payloads.py, app.py, server.py), templates/console.html, static/console_actions.js, `main.py --console [--console-port N]`, requirements-console.txt, tests/test_con1_operator_console_read_only.py (AC-1..AC-11). Fixed three pre-existing eager vendor-package imports (utils/config_ui.py, utils/config_history.py, utils/crypto_posture.py each imported `configuration.*` at module load time) to lazy/at-point-of-use, required for AC-8 (console/ must transitively import no checkpoint/*, panorama/*, configuration/* module) -- behavior-preserving for every other caller. CON.1's human interactive real-browser open (same session, 2026-09-01): live-drove the console against the uitest fixture in a real Chromium tab through all seven modules -- zero console errors, real data rendered -- and along the way found and fixed two regressions the automated suite/render-harness missed: (1) three JS-set inline style="" attributes (compliance_ui.js's segmented coverage bar, project_plan_ui.js's roadmap progress bar) were blocked outright by the console's stricter CSP (style-src 'self', no unsafe-inline) -- the static report's CSP kept unsafe-inline so never hit this; replaced with a fixed w-pct-0..w-pct-100 class set (static/style.css); (2) inventory_ui.js/configuration_ui.js/compliance_ui.js each computed a derived collection (inventory, configDevices, complianceSubjects) exactly once at module-load time against the still-empty default payload, before initializeReport(payloads) assigns the real one -- affected the exported static report too, not just the console; fixed with rebuildX() functions called both at load and from initializeReport. Status: DONE. C-D3 (Provenance.CONSOLE vs reusing 'manual') RESOLVED 2026-09-01, product owner chose add 'console' per the on-file recommendation. CON.2 SHIPPED 2026-09-01 same session: utils/collection_executor.py gained workflow_argv() (promoted out of application/workflows/maintenance.py's _scheduler_workflow_argv, now a one-line wrapper over it -- scheduler and console share one argv construction path, C2-2); utils/coordinator_backend.py gained Provenance.CONSOLE = 'console' (C2-3) -- audited every consumer (Job, RunContext, both coordinator backends' Postgres TEXT column, the discovery/coordinator UI payload) and found each already stores/echoes provenance as a free string with no fixed-value validation, so this was purely additive, no schema or consumer change needed; utils/evidence_backend.py gained a sixth storage concern (ConsoleJobBackend, filesystem + opt-in Postgres, same pattern as DEV.3.3's five) for durable job records under data_root/state/console_jobs; new console/registry.py (JOB_REGISTRY, seven job types per C2-1, including cp_gaia_backup declared but refused per C2-6), console/jobs.py (ConsoleJobStore -- idempotency C2-9, crash recovery C2-5, forbidden-field enforcement by construction C2-4), console/runner.py (single-worker FIFO executor, C2-7, calls main.main() only -- AC-2 -- never a collector or vendor module); console/app.py gained POST /api/jobs, GET /api/jobs, GET /api/jobs/{id}, GET /api/jobs/{id}/events (SSE, C2-10), GET /api/job-types -- create_app()'s job_store/runner params are optional (auto-constructed) so CON.1's existing test fixture and any read-only-only caller keep working unmodified; static/console_actions.js gained the action surface (job-type buttons, jobs table, an SSE reader implemented via fetch()+ReadableStream since native EventSource cannot carry the Authorization bearer header) in templates/console.html's Discovery module. New tests/test_con2_console_job_engine.py (26 tests, AC-1..AC-11 plus C2-1/C2-3 coverage); tests/test_con1_operator_console_read_only.py's AC-2 route-table test updated in place to allow the one deliberate POST /api/jobs route CON.2 adds. items.title: CP preflight: add `cphaprob tablestat` (CCP unique-IP table) as an extra split-brain / control-link evidence source
items.priority: P1 -- valuable evidence, requires a new command-gate row + readiness-contract mapping before implementation
items.target: OP.0b follow-on (post S8 closure); implement only after PO approval of the gate row and the check mapping
items.note: PO request 2026-09-04 (real-environment ClusterXL S8-A, operator-supplied evidence). VENDOR SEMANTIC: `cphaprob tablestat` prints the CCP 'Unique IP's Table' -- for each cluster interface, which members are currently seen exchanging CCP on it (local member rows plus peer member rows, with per-interface IP and MAC). It answers a question the approved battery cannot: `cphaprob -a if` (CP-A4) proves the LOCAL link state of each cluster interface, not that CCP traffic is actually flowing to the peer on it. Operator scenario: one cluster interface physically disconnected while its link reports UP -- `cphaprob -a if` and `cphaprob stat` still look healthy, but the peer's row for that interface disappears from tablestat; that is the precursor to a split-brain election. So tablestat is positive, per-interface, cross-member CCP reachability evidence. WHY NOT ADDED NOW: it is a NEW device command, which is a hard-stop condition of the S8 campaign (new command authority = PO gate, `OP_0B_1_COMMAND_GATE_PACKAGE.md`), and its readiness mapping is a readiness-contract decision, not a parser fix. Nothing in the approved battery changed; `cphaprob -a if` (A4) and `cphaprob -ia list` (A5) are already approved reads and both now parse the real output shapes. WHAT IMPLEMENTATION NEEDS: (1) a gate row modelled on CP-A4 -- Vendor Check Point; Action class CLASS_0_READ; Execution plane device-direct SSH, existing per-member persistent Expert shell; Shell/context Expert direct, physical/VS0; Expected calls per member 1; Concurrency/timeout/retry as CP-A4 (NO_RETRY); Session reuse yes, same session and same INTER_COMMAND_DELAY_SECONDS pacing; Read-only evidence yes (`cphaprob tablestat` is a ClusterXL monitoring command); Evidence category F (link/control health) and/or the split-brain category. (2) SAFE RETAINED FIELDS ONLY -- the raw table carries per-interface IP addresses and MAC addresses: the parser must retain NO address, NO MAC, NO interface name; only bounded counts/booleans: number of cluster interfaces observed, number on which BOTH members are seen, number on which the peer member is absent, and whether the local member is seen on every required interface (cross-referenced only by count against CP-A4's `Required interfaces:`). Structural skeleton diagnostic applies if the shape is unrecognised. (3) READINESS MAPPING (PO decision, not to be invented): candidate checks are `no_split_brain` (peer absent on a required cluster interface = CCP not exchanged = election risk) and `control_sync_link_health` (per-interface CCP reachability, stronger than link state). The classification of 'peer row absent on a required interface' -- FAIL versus INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE -- must be decided against the frozen 'never KNOWN_BAD from absence' law: here the absence is inside the device's own positively-reported table, which is a different thing from a read that produced nothing, but the contract must say so explicitly before the code does. (4) VSX: physical/VS0 context only unless a per-VS semantic is separately established. (5) Tests: parser fail-closed on unknown shape; value-free retained fields (no IP/MAC survives); one call per member in the same shell; battery order and S4 command authority unchanged. Until this item is implemented, the readiness contract keeps its current (weaker) control-link evidence: link state, not CCP exchange.

items.title: Per-HA-entity operational lock -- the CLASS 2 lock grain does not exist
items.note: Closes the OP.0b.0 frozen contract's own bug/gap register row X-1 (docs/history/phase/OP_0B_0_VENDOR_FAILOVER_PREFLIGHT_EVIDENCE_SURFACE.md section 26: 'per-HA-entity lock (10.1 item 4) tracked nowhere ... P0 before CLASS 2 (record now)'), which had no backlog item, no roadmap row and no design section anywhere in the repository. FAILOVER_ENGINE_ARCHITECTURE.md section 10.1 item 4 requires a per-HA-entity lock held across preflight -> act -> verify. The lock that exists today is per PHYSICAL ENDPOINT -- utils.coordinator_backend.derive_lock_key(secret, 'endpoint', canonical_id), admitted by utils.collection_executor.CollectionCoordinator -- and two members of one cluster are two endpoints, so it is the wrong grain for an action whose subject is the cluster. MODEL (independent review 2026-09-04, docs/history/phase/OP_2_0_CONTROLLED_HA_OPERATION_ARCHITECTURE.md P8/P10): (1) the HA-entity lock IS the durable action record -- the store admits at most one record per operational_entity_id (CP ClusterXL group_id; CP VSX physical cluster parent; never a member, management address, SSH endpoint, API session or browser session) that is non-terminal or an unacknowledged OUTCOME_UNKNOWN, enforced by a create-race-safe uniqueness check; no new lock mechanism, key domain or table; (2) the existing per-endpoint coordinator admission (lease + vendor budget) is taken per device-contact stage -- the preflight, then precondition + submission + verification -- and NEVER across the human confirmation wait, because the lease is connection-lifetime (DEV.3.2) and the vendor budget (capacity 1) would otherwise block every collection of that vendor for an unbounded time; refused admission is ABORTED_PRE_MUTATION:member_busy, never a wait; (3) quarantine after OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is a derived predicate over the record store, lifted only by an authorized, audited acknowledgement -- a restart cannot lift it because reconciliation never rewrites a terminal state. Frozen by the product owner on 2026-09-04; implementation is OP.2.B's, a future movement behind OP.0b closure. CLOSED 2026-09-04: implemented in utils/operate/store.py (ActionRecordStore) exactly per the MODEL above -- see docs/history/phase/OP_2_A_B_EXECUTION_FOUNDATION.md.
